description.text: SailPoint, Inc. (together with its consolidated subsidiaries, as appropriate, “SailPoint,” the “Company,” “our,” or “we”) delivers solutions to enable adaptive identity security for the enterprise. We do this via the SailPoint Platform that unifies identity data across systems and identity types, including employee identities, non-employee identities, machine identities, and AI agents for real-time governance. Our SaaS and customer-hosted offerings leverage intelligent analytics to provide organizations with critical visibility into which identities currently have access to which resources, which identities should have access to those resources, and how that access is being used. Our solutions enable organizations to establish, control, and automate policies that help them define and maintain a robust security posture and achieve regulatory compliance. Powered by AI, our solutions enable organizations to overcome the scale and complexity of managing identities in real-time across dynamic, complex IT environments. The evolving threat landscape requires a more adaptive, context-aware identity security approach than ever before. The number of cyber attacks continues to increase at an accelerating rate, fueled in part by the adoption of AI by threat actors. This has lowered the barrier for sophisticated attacks and enabled threat actors to scale their efforts with unprecedented efficiency.

about.description_short: SailPoint (Nasdaq: SAIL) is defining the new era of adaptive identity security. In a world where non-human identities now significantly outnumber humans, our AI-powered platform unifies identity, security, and data intelligence to protect today's enterprise from advanced identity-based threats. We deliver the identity solution that spans both the breadth of identities and the depth of context needed to drive real-time access with confidence. Built on principles like zero-standing privilege and contextualized risk, our SailPoint platform transforms identity from a point of vulnerability into a powerful security advantage. Trusted by many of the world's leading organizations, SailPoint secures the enterprise with intelligent, autonomous identity security.

analysis_md:
# SAIL — SailPoint, Inc.
Engine 5.4 run, 2026-10-18. **In scope** (market cap $10.203B at $18.75, nasdaq_quote_api — under the $40B scope cap). US filer on Form 10-K (FY2026 ended 2026-01-31, filed 2026-03-19), USD. No overrides — no data gaps.

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv, or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
The category leader in identity governance and administration (IGA): SailPoint's platform answers "who — human, machine, or AI agent — should have access to what" for large enterprises: access certification campaigns, lifecycle provisioning, and policy enforcement, layered on top of whichever identity anchor (Microsoft Entra, Okta) the customer runs. Founded 2005, taken private by Thoma Bravo in 2022, re-IPO'd February 2025 (Thoma Bravo retains a majority — a controlled company). ~3,235 customers per company filings. The business is mid-transition from term licenses to SaaS: Q2 FY2027 (reported 2026-09-09) total ARR $1.231B, +25% YoY; SaaS ARR $847M, +36%, 97% of net new ARR; AI/agentic-identity ARR above $70M; dollar-based net retention 113%, gross retention high-90s; FY2027 ARR guidance raised to $1.38B with ~$200M free cash flow guided. In June 2026 it closed the Entro Security acquisition (non-human identity; ~$200M per press reports, terms undisclosed).

## Owner's earnings
**FY2026 (10-K via EDGAR):** operating cash flow $70,580,000 — the first positive OCF year in this CIK's history; capex $5,980,000; SBC $254,872,000 (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2026: -$190,272,000 = -$0.35/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $-0.35). Free cash flow was +$64,600,000; SBC alone consumed it ~3.9 times over.
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): **-$98,120,000** for FY2026 per financials_history.csv — negative on both definitions.
- OE positive **0 of the last 3** fiscal years. Per-year conservative OE/share (financials_history.csv): FY2024 -$3.60, FY2025 -$1.71, FY2026 -$0.35 — improving fast, still negative. The early years were under the Thoma Bravo LBO capital structure (FY2024 interest expense $187,059,000 in fundamentals.json); the FY2026 SBC step-up ($31,714,000 in FY2025 → $254,872,000) is the post-IPO equity-comp reset, and it is what keeps OE negative now that OCF has turned.
- **Base used = the TTM pin from ttm.json: -$0.08/share** (base_source: ttm_json). TTM legs (ttm.json, through 2026-07-31): OCF $200,646,000 (FY $70,580,000 − prior YTD -$46,862,000 + current YTD $83,204,000) − capex $5,730,000 − SBC $238,237,000 = **TTM OE -$43,321,000** on 566,360,000 diluted shares. Normalized 3-yr median base: **-$1.71/share**. Every defensible base is negative; the freshest one is closest to zero, which is the whole story in one line.
- Balance sheet (latest FY, key_numbers.md / financials_history.csv): cash $358,144,000, total debt $0 (the FY2025 long-term debt of $1,024,467,000 was repaid out of the IPO), **net debt -$358.1M — net cash** (basis TOTAL:LongTermDebt), lease liabilities $18,081,000. Book equity $6,846,231,000 post-IPO vs -$5,588,440,000 pre-IPO.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate/narrow, leadership real, economics unproven
Justification: SailPoint is the recognized leader in identity governance and administration (IGA) — the governance layer enterprises buy on top of whichever identity anchor (Microsoft Entra, Okta) they run — with compliance-mandated switching costs: access-certification and lifecycle workflows are embedded in regulated-industry audit processes and implementations run for years. Retention confirms it: dollar-based net retention 113% and gross retention in the high 90s (Q2 FY2027 reporting), ARR $1.231B growing 25%, SaaS ARR +36% to $847M. But there is no demonstrated return on capital: operating income is negative in every filed year, conservative owner's earnings are negative 0 of 3 filed years and on TTM, and the roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json (+34.9% FY2024, +3.2% FY2025, -3.7% FY2026) is denominator noise from the Thoma Bravo LBO (negative book equity pre-IPO) and the February 2025 re-IPO recapitalization, with D&A of $211-264M/yr dominated by amortization of acquisition intangibles. Gross margin (60.5% FY2024 → 64.5% FY2025 → 64.5% FY2026 → 66.2% TTM) is improving but mid-pack for SaaS, not an elite pricing-power signature. Microsoft bundling Entra governance into M365 is the standing erosion force, with Okta, CyberArk (now Palo Alto Networks), Saviynt and AI-native entrants converging on the same agentic-identity ground. A 5 gives CAP 8.5 years.
- FOR: Category leader in identity governance (IGA) — rated best-tier for governance in 2026 buyer comparisons; ~3,235 customers per company filings. Compliance-mandated switching costs: access-certification and lifecycle workflows embedded in regulated-industry audit processes; implementations are multi-year and painful to rip out. Retention in the numbers: dollar-based net retention 113%, gross retention in the high 90s (Q2 FY2027). SaaS transition compounding: SaaS ARR +36% YoY to $847M and 97% of net new ARR; AI/agentic-identity ARR above $70M with a pipeline above $200M.
- AGAINST: No demonstrated returns on capital: operating losses every filed year, conservative OE negative 0/3 filed years and on TTM; roic_proxy is LBO/IPO denominator noise, not a through-cycle ROIC record. Microsoft Entra bundles governance into the M365 relationship — the strategically decisive competitor; Okta, CyberArk/Palo Alto, Saviynt and AI-native vendors converge from every layer. SBC is a heavy recurring cost: $238.2M TTM (~20% of TTM revenue), exceeding TTM free cash flow of $194.9M; post-IPO diluted share count still rising (544.2M FY2026 → 566.4M YTD FY2027). Gross margin 64.5% (FY2025-26) is mid-pack for SaaS — term-license and services mix, no elite pricing-power signature yet. Controlled company: Thoma Bravo retains a majority stake; the June 2026 Entro acquisition (~$200M reported) adds integration risk in non-human identity.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection. (Moot for the score — see DCF.)

## DCF — Tier F: no scenario table exists, and that is the finding
The engine's Tier F branch fired on both the preliminary run (normalized median base) and the final TTM-pinned run: no scenarios, IVs, or IRRs are computed (implied_irr_weighted: null). Probabilities recorded for the run: 10/25/30/25/10 (defaults — nothing in the evidence justifies tilting weights for a branch that does not use them).
- **F sub-type: sbc_exceeds_cash** (f_subtype_basis: ttm.json legs, TTM pin). The TTM cash generation is real and positive — OCF $200,646,000 − capex $5,730,000 = $194,916,000 of free cash flow (fundamentals.json TTM fcf agrees) — and SBC of $238,237,000 consumes all of it and $43.3M more. On the unpinned preliminary run the sub-type read no_cash_generation (3-yr window sum of OCF − capex is negative: FY2024 -$252,931,000, FY2025 -$111,753,000, FY2026 +$64,600,000 per financials_history.csv); the TTM pin is the fresher and more precise diagnosis.
- **Growth sanity check:** the engine's blend is 18.74% (key_numbers.md: rev CAGR 5y 23.74%, 3y 23.74%, latest rev YoY 24.35%, after the -5.00pp share-count adjustment). Scenario starts on that blend would be super bear 6.74% / bear 13.74% / base 18.74% / bull 23.74% / super bull 30.74%. Against the prints: FY2026 revenue +24.35% YoY, TTM revenue +20.13% YoY (fundamentals.json), Q2 FY2027 revenue +17% YoY but ARR +25% and SaaS ARR +36%. Written reason for the base start sitting above the latest quarterly revenue print: reported revenue growth is depressed by the term-to-SaaS mix shift (point-in-time license revenue shrinking as migrations complete); ARR is the truer demand gauge and supports the blend. The -5pp dilution adjustment is separately too harsh — see DILUTION below. None of it matters to the tier: growth applied to a negative base produces no valuation in any case.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest FY ended 2026-01-31, ~9 months ago): ttm.py was run and the final engine pass pins the TTM base from it (base_source: ttm_json). TTM legs quoted in Owner's earnings above: OCF $200,646,000, capex $5,730,000, SBC $238,237,000, shares 566,360,000 → TTM OE -$43,321,000, -$0.08/share. The TTM base is still negative, so the pin sharpens the diagnosis (sbc_exceeds_cash) without changing the tier.
- **DILUTION** (share count CAGR 159.43%): an artifact of the re-IPO, not economic dilution of public holders. FY2024–25 diluted counts (80,746,000 / 83,716,000 in financials_history.csv) are the pre-IPO SailPoint Parent, LP unit structure; the February 2025 IPO conversion produced the ~544,159,000-share public count. The engine's -5.00pp growth adjustment therefore over-penalizes history. The real, current dilution is SBC-driven and much smaller: diluted shares 544,159,000 (FY2026) → 566,360,000 (YTD FY2027 weighted), shares outstanding 570,911,633 at 2026-09-04 — roughly a 4%/yr pace, funded by the $238.2M TTM SBC. Immaterial to an F verdict either way.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (FY2026: net income -$270,054,000 vs OCF +$70,580,000): no one-off tax deposit, impairment, or working-capital swing is needed to explain it — the gap is structural non-cash charges. SBC of $254,872,000 and D&A of $210,774,000 (financials_history.csv; the D&A is dominated by amortization of the intangibles created in Thoma Bravo's 2022 acquisition) are added back in the cash-flow statement and together exceed the entire divergence. The OCF-based conservative OE is the right series — and after deducting that same SBC as a real cost, it is negative.
- **THIN_HISTORY** (only 3 fiscal years): this CIK's filed history begins FY2024 and spans three different companies in effect — LBO-owned (FY2024–25, negative book equity, $1.0B+ of acquisition debt), the February 2025 IPO recapitalization, and the post-IPO public company (FY2026). The predecessor's 2017–2022 public history sits under a different registrant and is not in these facts. Every cross-year comparison (share count, SBC, interest, equity, ROIC) straddles that break; confidence is capped at low for exactly this reason. The F verdict itself does not depend on the broken comparisons — OE is negative inside each regime separately.

## My thoughts / overlay
- There is no method range to hide behind: normalized-median base -$1.71/share, latest-FY-only -$0.35/share, TTM -$0.08/share, maintenance-definition FY2026 -$98,120,000. Every defensible variant is Tier F. Anyone quoting a DCF value for SAIL today is projecting SBC normalization, not measuring owner's earnings.
- The trajectory is genuinely close to the flip, and the flip condition is precise: TTM free cash flow is already +$194.9M and management guides ~$200M FCF for FY2027 — owner's earnings turn positive the moment SBC falls below OCF − capex. SBC is already drifting the right way ($254.9M FY2026 → $238.2M TTM, and H1 FY2027 SBC of $137,426,000 vs $154,061,000 in H1 FY2026 per ttm.json legs), but at ~20% of revenue it has a long way to fall, and the post-IPO share count is still rising ~4%/yr while it does.
- The franchise evidence is real: ARR +25%, SaaS ARR +36%, NRR 113%, gross margin expanding to 66.2% TTM, net cash balance sheet after the IPO repaid the LBO debt. What the $18.75 price ($10.203B market cap, ~8.8x TTM revenue of $1,165,544,000 per fundamentals.json) is paying for is the agentic-identity option — AI-driven ARR above $70M, a $200M+ pipeline, the Entro deal — in a category where Microsoft gives a competing answer away inside M365. That is a growth-equity bet, not an owner's-earnings discount; this screen prices the second and finds nothing to price.
- What would change the tier: one filed period — FY2027's 10-K (expected March 2027) or a TTM window before it — in which OCF − capex − SBC prints positive. On current legs the gap is only $43.3M TTM, so a refresh on the FY2027 10-K is the trigger; the 3-yr median base will lag the flip by years, so a positive latest-year print should prompt an immediate re-score rather than waiting for the queue.

## Data / enrichment notes
- Enrichment (step 9) all ran: fundamentals.json, prices.json (421 closes back to the 2025-02-13 IPO), segments.json (product + geography tables, complete), statements.json, profile.json (description from the 10-K Item 1; 3,229 employees; no warnings) and street.json (consensus Buy, target $22.42 — a cache file, not scored) written. Non-blocking notes: segments.py dropped the parent "Subscription" member rows (definition-linkbase parents of the SaaS / term / maintenance children); statements.py flags basis breaks on a few quarterly lines (net_income_to_common FY2025, deferred taxes and capex_intangibles captions) across filing generations — none touch the annual OE legs. reprice.py skipped SAIL by design — Tier F names have no IRR to reprice (no live.json).
- No dividends (fundamentals.json: not a dividend payer), no buybacks filed; share issuance is the SBC/IPO flow only.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: F** (tier by numbers F, sub-type sbc_exceeds_cash on the TTM pin; no tier override)
